article.headline: No. 16 Duke beats No. 10 UConn 77-63 as John Blackwell scores 25
article.description: — John Blackwell scored 20 of his 25 points in the second half and No. 16 Duke defeated No. 10 Connecticut 77-63 on Wednesday night in an Elite Eight rematch.
article.story: LAS VEGAS -- — John Blackwell scored 20 of his 25 points in the second half and No. 16 Duke defeated No. 10 Connecticut 77-63 on Wednesday night in an Elite Eight rematch. Blackwell made 7 of 11 shots, including 5 of 6 from the 3-point arc to lead the Blue Devils (5-2). Patrick Ngongba II added 17 points, Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje scored 12 and Cayden Boozer had 10. The more balanced Blue Devils shot 52.2%, but Dame Sarr — who had six points and eight rebounds — went out with an apparent left leg injury with 5:26 left. Sarr helped shut down Silas Demary Jr. after a hot start for the UConn guard. He scored 25 points, but only a single free throw in the final 18:02. The Huskies (4-2) also got little help from anyone else. UConn just 11 of 48 shots outside of Demary. Braylon Mullins led the Big East Conference at a 20.8 points per game entering the night but made just 4 of 12 shots in scoring 12 points and battling foul trouble. The teams met last March, with UConn edging the Blue Devils 73-72 on Mullins' 3-pointer with 0.4 seconds left to advance to the Final Four. The tradition-rich programs have combined to win 11 national championships since 1991, with the coach Dan Hurley and the Huskies claiming the 2023 title after winning the regional in this same T-Mobile Arena. The game lost a little bit of the pregame hype when Duke lost by six points to now No. 11 Michigan State and 21 to now No. 4 Illinois to drop from its No. 2 preseason ranking. UConn was ranked fourth, but fell after losing by six points to now No. 8 Arizona. This game was a chance for both schools to show the preseason expectations were accurate, and it was Duke that threw the first punch with a 12-point run in the first half to go up 23-14. The Blue Devils led for more than 31 minutes to make an early-season statement. Up next Duke: At No. 3 Florida in the ACC/SEC Challenge on Tuesday night.
